subject: Implementation runway: streaming + tool-calling + structured-output schema alignment
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Ruiz <natalie@NimbusHealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Implementation runway: streaming + tool-calling + structured-output schema alignment

Hi Natalie —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To keep momentum we want to lock a short mutual action plan focused on three deliverables you called out: streaming responses for live triage, function/tool-calling for downstream EHR lookups, and structured JSON outputs for the intake pipeline.

Proposed 3-point runway:
- Week 1: Schema alignment (we send a draft schema & sample responses)
- Week 2: Dev integration (streaming & tool-call hooks; small proxy test)
- Week 3: Staging validation & go/no-go for limited rollout

I attached a lightweight checklist and a first-pass schema draft (see nimbus_streaming-schema-v1.json). Can you confirm the right DevOps point-of-contact and whether there are any constraints on outgoing webhook endpoints from your VPC?

Next steps: if you confirm the DevOps email and availability, I’ll book a 30-min implementation sync (technical + CS) early next week.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: nimbus_onboarding-checklist.xlsx, nimbus_streaming-schema-v1.json

Karthik —

Sounds good. I’ve looped in our DevOps alias (devops@nimbushealth.com). Carlos (cc’d on follow-up) will be the engineer driving the integration. A couple quick notes from our side:
- Outgoing webhook policy: we allow HTTPS to whitelisted endpoints; will need the Redwood callback host and cert info.
- For structured output, we want a compact keyset — patient_id, encounter_id, triage_code, and confidence.

I’m available for a 30-min sync Monday or Tuesday afternoon PT. Monday 2pm PT works best for Carlos and me.

—Natalie
Director of Product | Nimbus Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Ruiz <natalie@NimbusHealth.com>, Carlos Medina <carlos.medina@NimbusHealth.com>

Subject: Re: Implementation runway: streaming + tool-calling + structured-output schema alignment

Natalie / Carlos —

Great, appreciate the quick reply and the policy note. I’ve turned the proposed runway into a runnable mutual action plan below and attached a compact onboarding checklist for your PM/Eng leads (nimbus_onboarding-checklist.xlsx).

Mutual action plan (high level)
1) Schema sign-off (this week)
   - Redwood: provide compact JSON schema + sample responses (attached schema v1 and sample-responses)
   - Nimbus: review & mark fields required/optional; confirm patient/encounter mapping
2) Dev integration (week 2)
   - Provide RFC for streaming endpoint (chunked responses + reconnect semantics)
   - Tool-calling: outline a single EHR lookup call we can wire via function/tool-calling; we’ll ship a simulator for local testing
3) Validation & pilot (week 3)
   - Redwood will run a small data set through staging; Nimbus will validate structured outputs and sign-off on go/no-go metrics (matching keys + confidence thresholds)

Open questions for the sync:
- Carlos: can you confirm the allowed cipher suites and whether mutual TLS is required?
- Natalie: do you have an existing validation harness (JSON Schema validator) we should run against? If not, Redwood can share a simple Node/Python harness.

I’ll schedule the Monday 2pm PT slot for a 30-min technical sync and include a short agenda (schema review, streaming hooks, tool-call flow, next steps).

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: nimbus_onboarding-checklist.xlsx, nimbus_sample-responses.json

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Natalie Ruiz <natalie@NimbusHealth.com>, Carlos Medina <carlos.medina@NimbusHealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation runway: streaming + tool-calling + structured-output schema alignment

Folks —

Technical notes for the Monday sync (short):
- Streaming semantics: Redwood supports SSE-style chunking and chunk-level metadata (sequence id, partial KVs). For reconnects we supply an ephemeral resume token for the KV cache to avoid re-computation on large contexts.
- Tool-calling: Recommend a single POST /ehr/lookup with a JSON body {"patient_id": "", "lookup_keys": ["ssn","mrn"]} that returns a compact object; Redwood function calls surface the result as a typed structure to the model runtime.
- JSON Schema: the attached nimbus_streaming-schema-v1.json is intentionally minimal. We added a top-level envelope: {"record_version","payload"} — please flag any fields you require in the payload section.

Validation harness: we’ve put a small validator and sample test cases in the shared Drive folder (link above). If Nimbus prefers, Dylan can drop a short CI snippet to run on your side to auto-validate staging commits.

One gotcha we’ve seen: when confidence thresholds are close to the binary decision boundary, structured-output mappings can flip for short prompts. We recommend adding an explicit confidence floor in the schema (confidence >= 0.20) during pilot.

Attaching sample-responses file for the schema validator.

—Monica
Sr. Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachments: nimbus_streaming-schema-v1.json, nimbus_sample-responses.json

Thanks everyone — short summary and explicit asks before Monday: 

Decisions so far:
- Monday 2:00pm PT confirmed for 30-min implementation sync.
- Schema v1 attached; Redwood will treat confidence floor as suggestion unless Nimbus specifies otherwise.
- Endpoint requirements: Redwood will provision a callback host and cert details prior to sync; Carlos, please confirm if mTLS will be required.

Asks for Monday
1) Carlos: confirm mTLS requirement and allowed cipher list (reply if you can before the sync).
2) Natalie: confirm whether the four keys we proposed (patient_id, encounter_id, triage_code, confidence) are sufficient for the intake pipeline or whether you need extra fields (e.g., provider_id).
3) Nimbus: please review the onboarding checklist and sign the DocuSign (linked) if the timeline looks good — we’ll treat that as the mutual action plan baseline.

I’ve attached a short demo recording (demo-recording-20260709.mp4) showing the streaming behavior and a quick example of a function/tool call wired to a fake EHR. If anyone needs the raw screencast, let me know and I’ll upload to Drive.

If there are no further blockers we’ll use the Monday sync to finalize field-level sign-off and hand off to Carlos for the integration sprint.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: demo-recording-20260709.mp4
